shared_elements: standing richly costumed human figure dominating the field
blocks of square hieroglyph-like signs arranged in columns/grid
small subsidiary figure at lower level near the main figure's feet
low-relief carving on a rectangular slab with framing border
justification: Both show a single ornately dressed standing personage with a towering plumed headdress, beaded pectoral and fringed kilt, accompanied by a small subordinate figure at the lower level and by grids of square glyph-like sign blocks — a very specific and arbitrary combination unlikely to arise independently, rendered in the same shallow, densely textured relief with the same crowded infill conventions. The main differences are orientation and layout: A's figure is in profile with glyph columns framing him on both sides in a wide panel, while B's figure is nearly frontal on a tall slab with the glyph blocks confined to one lower side and a bound captive in a basal register.
